title: Skipped last year's FHSA? Your room can be $16,000.
made_by: 엔진/find.py 2026-11-04 · 신호 ['s53720468'] · 퍼스나 The late starter with unused room

fact.thing: maximum FHSA participation room in the second year when nothing was put in the first year
fact.claim: In the year you open your first FHSA you get $8,000 of participation room. Each later year adds another $8,000, and up to $8,000 of room you did not use can carry into the next year. So if you opened an FHSA last year and put nothing in, your room this year can be $16,000, and the contributions can be claimed as a tax deduction. Unused room only starts carrying forward once an FHSA is open, the carry-forward is capped at $8,000, and the lifetime limit is $40,000.
sources: CRA TAX TIP – Make the most of your FHSA

plain.what: An FHSA is a First Home Savings Account. It is a savings box for your first home, and money you put in can lower your tax. Each year the box is open gives you $8,000 of room, and up to $8,000 of room you didn't use waits for you in the next year.
plain.so_what: If you opened one last year and put in $0, your room this year can be $16,000 instead of $8,000.
plain.do: Look up your FHSA room on your CRA notice of assessment and write the number down.
